clue.text: Recently taken photographs showing smart guys?

definitions.meaning: pictures that are fresh off the camera would be ..., hot meaning new
show-offs who are very skilled or successful, the question mark flagging the playful pairing

explanation.surface: A caption asking whether a set of fresh snaps shows off some well-dressed men.
explanation.definitionFit: A single compound noun for skilled, flashy high achievers, also readable as new photographs.

clue.text: Operative and I cover obstacle

parts.note: a hand is a worker, an operative
a cap is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: A worker and the speaker cover up a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hindrance or disadvantage that impedes progress.

clue.text: Played out, even round river

indicators.note: the word for even goes round the river letter

parts.note: a tied score is an even one
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A match finishes level after a round by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: played out means exhausted, worn out.

clue.text: The man circling round floor presenting dance

indicators.note: the pronoun for the man circles the round letter

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
O is round in shape
to floor someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: A man twirls round the floor at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lively American country dance or the social gathering where it is held.

clue.text: Some shown up in bunker

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Some people are shown up in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunker is golf's sand trap, a hazard on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in golf, a bunker is a sand hazard also called by this name.

clue.text: Heedless, bishop put a match to explosive

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to put a match to something is to set it alight, so lit
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A careless clergyman cheerfully lights a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone carefree and casual pays no heed to consequences.

clue.text: Branagh's lead in 'Hamlet' excited London borough

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed up
the lead of Branagh's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Kenneth Branagh's starring turn in Hamlet thrilled a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like an acting role, but gives B, which 'excited' mixes with HAMLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a borough of south London, home of the Archbishop of Canterbury's palace.

clue.text: Fare for Italians to get here?

definitions.text: Fare for Italians to get here?

parts.words: Fare for Italians to get here?
parts.note: fare looks like a ticket price for a journey, but means food: Italian food is served at this place

explanation.surface: Asking about the ticket price for Italians travelling somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' wants to be a travel charge; it is food, so the place is where Italian dishes are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a simple Italian restaurant serving Italian food.

clue.text: Unabridged in content, I realised

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone realises a book's text is uncut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: whole, complete, with nothing cut out.

clue.text: She may attend to a babe in arms due to be changed

definitions.text: She may attend to a babe

indicators.note: the words in arms due are to be altered into a new order, like a nappy being changed

explanation.surface: A carer is holding a baby who is due for a nappy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In arms' looks like part of the definition, but it begins the anagram fodder; 'to be changed' rearranges IN ARMS DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a woman employed to look after small children would tend to an infant.

clue.text: Old fogey around is in need of treatment

indicators.note: words in need of treatment are to be worked on, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly bore around here needs medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a person with outdated views, as extinct as a prehistoric reptile.

clue.text: Had in mind poor time

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby, as in mean streets

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having thought of a bad moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something intended or planned is what a person had in view.

clue.text: Party held by trendy men under a roof

indicators.note: the word for party sits inside, held between the other two pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers, i.e. men
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party hosted by fashionable chaps takes place inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for something sheltered within a building, such as a pool or game played inside.

clue.text: Forebear — no trace, regrettably, across South

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stretch across, enclosing the letter for South
things gone regrettably wrong are disordered, so the letters of no trace are rearranged

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A sad note that no record of a forebear survives in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regrettably' rearranges NO TRACE into ANCETOR, which goes 'across' S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forebear is a forefather, someone from whom a person descends.

clue.text: Skirt round crew on stage

parts.note: a side is a team, a crew
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A stage crew walking round the edge of the set.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to avoid or evade an issue rather than face it.

clue.text: German dog in fine French spa, barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, crazy, so the letters of fine French spa are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dog is yapping at an elegant spa resort in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise but is British slang for mad, signalling the anagram of FINE FRENCH SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small, monkey-faced terrier-like toy breed originating in Germany.

clue.text: Apparent worth of clock prize

parts.note: clock is slang for face, as in to clock someone's mug, and a clock has a face
to prize something is to value it

explanation.surface: The worth of a clock awarded as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the seeming worth of something on the surface, as in take at face value.

clue.text: Supporter of that woman during a depression

indicators.note: the pronoun comes during, inside, the other pieces

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A woman's backer falls into a slump.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a follower or devotee of a cause.

clue.text: A butcher and I in mix-up about a steak

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the single letter a
the words A butcher and I are in a mix-up, so their letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A confused butcher and customer argue over a steak order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in mix-up' rearranges A BUTCHER AND I into CHTEAUBRIAND, which wraps 'about' A after CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thick cut of beef tenderloin, a classic steak dish.

clue.text: Husband over in local, shiftily getting booze

indicators.note: the two letters go into the rearranged word
shiftily means evasively, shifting about, so local is rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A husband in his local pub sneakily gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British pub near home. 'shiftily' turns LOCAL into ALCOL, and O and H go 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Sort of music and drink to bring affinity

parts.note: rap is a genre of music
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Music and wine as a way to bond with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a close, harmonious relationship between people.

clue.text: Fox, fine female in pack

indicators.note: the two letters sit in the word for pack

parts.note: a bale is a bound pack of goods
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A fox and a fine vixen among a pack of hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal of the hunting surface, but it is a verb meaning to puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fox someone is to puzzle or confuse them.

clue.text: Recommend Scottish barrister

definitions.meaning: to urge or speak in favour of something
in Scotland a lawyer who pleads in the higher courts has this title

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer offering a recommendation.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to argue for; the noun is the Scottish term for a barrister.

clue.text: Scattered surplus, holding spades

indicators.note: the word for surplus holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: spare means extra, surplus
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Leftover garden tools including spades lie strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thinly spread or scattered, as in sparse vegetation.

clue.text: Check about key monarchy

indicators.note: the word for check goes about, around, the key letter

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Checking around for a key to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the period or rule of a sovereign.

clue.text: Male leaves unexpected gift for girl

indicators.note: the male letter leaves, is removed from, the word for unexpected gift

parts.note: manna from heaven is an unexpected blessing

explanation.surface: A man walks out, leaving a surprise present for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common girl's name.

clue.text: Disgusting dirt in lift distressed hospital

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or roughed up, so the letters of lift are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A grimy, broken-down lift in a struggling hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foul, disgusting muck or grime.

clue.text: Criticise the piper's son and me after one show

indicators.note: the word me comes after the numeral for one

parts.note: to pan a film or play is to criticise it harshly
in the nursery rhyme, Tom, Tom, the piper's son, stole a pig
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a nursery-rhyme character and themselves following a single performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son' is an English nursery rhyme. The answer is the British family Christmas stage show with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a theatrical entertainment, typically staged at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Fairly uniformly

definitions.meaning: in a level, regular way without variation

explanation.surface: Two adverbs side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb covers both impartially, as in evenly matched, and smoothly, as in spread evenly.

clue.text: Stickler, soldier holding tense talks at the front

indicators.note: the word for soldier holds the tense letter inside it

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: only the front letter of talks is taken

explanation.surface: A strict soldier holding tense negotiations on the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a strict disciplinarian who insists on rules being followed exactly.
